text:
ashley: Heads-up, seeing a p99 TTFT spike in west-eu around 02:15 UTC. Grafana panel shows a sharp jump aligned with redis-primary-2 evictions. https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ttft/ttft-token-dashboard?orgId=1&panelId=42 :eyes:

mike: On it. Any quick query you used to correlate with evictions?

ashley: Query I used: prometheus -> rate(kvcache_evictions_total{instance=~"redis-primary-2.*"}[5m]) and inference_ttft_seconds{region="west-eu"} p99 slice by model. Also saw tokens_processed_total dip at the same time.

sanjay: Can you paste the small log dump? want to check client side reconnects / retry bursts.

ashley: pastebin of extract: ```
2026-03-18T02:15:03Z redis-primary-2 WARN maxmemory: Evicted 128 keys (volatile-lru)
2026-03-18T02:15:04Z proxy-frontend-12 INFO cache-miss model=redwood-7b seq=1 req_id=...
2026-03-18T02:15:04Z inference-queue-3 DEBUG kvcache: miss, fetching weights from s3 fallback
2026-03-18T02:15:06Z gpu-worker-7 WARN cold-batch-tail delay=0.78s
```

lina: looks like a small eviction storm causing cache misses -> cold work -> p99 tail. How often does this repeat?

ashley: This is the 3rd such spike over 36 hours, timestamps: 02:15, 11:02, 19:47. Eviction rate pulses at redis-primary-2 only.

mike: Thoughts: 2 quick mitigations: 1) relax redis maxmemory-policy for that instance (or increase maxmemory), 2) temp route small fraction of traffic away from west-eu (canary) to see if p99 drops. Both have cost/latency tradeoffs.

sanjay: Before touching memory, we should confirm sampling bias in the TTFT panel. Our p99 is sensitive to bursts of 100-200 requests. The histogram binning in the dashboard is 50ms buckets which clips the tail. Suggest switching to microsecond buckets for the probe or using summary_quantile on the service side.

lina: Agreed on observability side: add an annotation on grafana for kvcache_evictions_total > 5 in 5m. Also add per-shard series for redis_memory_used_bytes to the panel.

opsbot: ALERT: kvcache_evictions_total high on redis-primary-2 (rate > 5 / 5m). Triggered at 2026-03-18T02:16:00Z. Alert severity: warning.

mike: opsbot noted it. I'll open a quick runbook step: increment redis maxmemory by 10% on redis-primary-2 and watch eviction rate for 15m. If not stable, revert and roll a second replica.

ashley: Before we change infra, a lower-risk test: adjust client-side KV caching TTLs to keep hot prefixes in local LRU for an extra 30s. That should reduce backend evictions during short bursts. We can flip via config flag on canary proxies.

sanjay: Also want to tweak the Grafana alert: we currently alert on p99 > 500ms for 2m. That fires on short cold tails and creates noise. Proposal: change to p99 > 600ms AND kvcache_evictions_total rate > 2 in 5m. That reduces false positives and ties the alert to the root cause.

lina: +1. Also add a derived metric for "cold_miss_count" exported by the proxy (proxy_cold_miss_total) and use that for future correlation.

mike: Quick mitigation in progress: canary proxy flag rolled to 5% traffic in west-eu to extend local TTL. Will monitor panels.

ashley: After canary flip, p99 dropped from ~820ms -> ~260ms for the 5% segment. Overall still shows a small bump but much narrower.

opsbot: NOTE: annotation added on Grafana for eviction event at 2026-03-18T02:15:03Z by mike

lina: Good signal. Action items: 1) change alert rule as sanjay suggested, 2) add eviction annotations for last 7d, 3) schedule a maintenance window to bump redis-primary-2 memory or redistribute shards.

mike: I'll create the alert PR and start a redis sizing ticket (infra#4521). Will also create a short runbook entry for this class of eviction-driven TTFT spikes.

ashley: For cost note: bumping redis memory increases infra cost, but cold misses are driving more GPU work & tokens/sec consumption per request. Rough calc: each cold miss adds ~0.5s GPU time => ~0.00014 GPU hours per request. At scale that beats the memory delta, we should include a cost projection in the ticket.

sanjay: I can produce a quick cost model: take tokens/sec per minute and overlay cold_miss_rate to estimate extra GPU-hours. Will post numbers in the ticket.

lina: Thanks team. If spike reappears after 24h with mitigations, we'll plan shard rebalance.

mike: marking done for immediate oncall actions. follow-ups: infra sizing ticket, grafana alert PR, proxy TTL rollback plan.

ashley: Closing thread for now — please ping if you see recurrence. :thumbsup:
